plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray, narrow leaves and dense spikes of fragrant purple flowers that attract bees and butterflies. Widely grown in gardens and commercial fields for essential oil production.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June to August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the United States
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years, and the Romans added it to their bathwater, which gave the plant its name from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large, bright flower head made up of yellow ray florets surrounding a dark disk of tiny seed-producing florets. Early varieties begin flowering in early July.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer to early fall (July to September)
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated widely in Ukraine, Russia, Argentina, and the United States
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds track the sun from east to west during the day (heliotropism), but mature flowers stop moving and face east.

plants.name: Hydrangea macrophylla
plants.description: A deciduous shrub with large rounded clusters of showy flowers. Flower color varies with soil acidity: acidic soils produce blue blooms, while alkaline soils produce pink ones.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer to early fall (June to September)
plants.location: Native to Japan; grown in temperate gardens in Europe, North America, and the Azores
plants.funFact: Aluminum availability in acidic soil is what turns the flowers blue, so gardeners can change the bloom color by adjusting soil pH.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with the largest flower heads in the Protea genus, up to 30 cm across, with pink-tipped bracts surrounding a central cone. In the Southern Hemisphere, it blooms in winter and spring, with some flowering in the cool months.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in South Africa, with scattered blooms from autumn to early spring (about May to November)
plants.location: Fynbos region of the Western Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: King Protea is South Africa's national flower and is one of the oldest flowering plants, with a lineage dating back about 300 million years.
